title: Chords: C, F and G Triads
description: The three primary chords of C major as root-position triads in both hands - the chords behind most beginner songs - held as whole notes, then halves, then quarters.

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: Root-position triads only (RH 1-3-5, LH 5-3-1), the same shape moved to C, F and G; speed increases from whole notes to quarter notes.
teachingPoints: Every triad is the same hand shape - thumb, middle finger, little finger on alternate white keys. Learn the shape on C, then slide it to F and G.
RH: C-E-G, F-A-C, G-B-D with 1-3-5; LH: C-E-G and F-A-C with 5-3-1, and the G chord drops to G2-B2-D3.
Play all three notes of a chord at exactly the same instant - listen for one sound, not a roll.
Bar 7 changes chord every beat: prepare the next shape in the air while the current chord sounds.
